I added the `flagged` subcommand to `skills/planning/critic/scripts/critic_ledger.py`. I ran it on five sample files and each gave the result you specified:

| Input | Result |
|---|---|
| Valid array wrapped in a ```` ```json ```` fence | prints the array as JSON, exit 0 |
| Valid array with no fence | not tested; the fence stripping is the same code `validate` uses, and nothing about a bare array differs |
| `{}` (not an array) | `FLAGGED_DECISIONS_PARSE_ERROR: expected a JSON array`, exit 1 |
| `[{"decision":"a"}]` (missing `why_flagged`) | `FLAGGED_DECISIONS_PARSE_ERROR: item 0 needs decision and why_flagged`, exit 1 |
| Invalid JSON (`x`) | `PARSE_ERROR: Expecting value: line 1 column 1 (char 0)`, exit 1 |
| Missing file | `PARSE_ERROR: [Errno 2] No such file or directory: 'nope'`, exit 1 |

It reuses the script's existing fence-stripping and JSON loading, so unreadable files and bad JSON produce the same `PARSE_ERROR:` line as `validate`. I also added `flagged` to the usage list in the module docstring. I didn't touch `SKILL.md`, so it doesn't mention the new subcommand.
